notes: KING/ETH Uniswap v4 pool; Base (8453) is the repository fork target, while launch configuration selects the deployment chain and PoolManager. KingToken is a plain ERC-20 with 1,000,000,000 KING, 18 decimals, minted once to its deployer. KingHook creates an immutable KingRouter. No owner powers, later minting, upgrades, pausing or mutable parameters. Only PoolManager can invoke enabled callbacks. Initialization binds one ETH/KING pool and accepts LP tiers 500/3000/10000; this pool uses 3000 (0.3%) and tick spacing 60. Transfers and liquidity changes have no hook callbacks. Every buy/sell pays an additional ETH hook fee in both exact modes, from buy input or sell output: 25% at initialization, falling linearly to 2.5% over 30 minutes. ETH-specified swaps reject partial fills; other fees use settled ETH deltas. Fees split 92% to the throne pool and 8% to 0x39E3414e7a43DE41675e9bEC52F7C9F6ae489CB6, with integer rounding. ERC-6909 ETH claims on PoolManager avoid prefunding ETH for fee collection on token-only launches. claim() redeems only the caller's credit under a reentrancy guard; a rejecting payee reverts its own claim without blocking fee collection. The throne pool has no discretionary withdrawal. The throne stays empty until 30 minutes end. A single KingRouter buy with gross ETH paid >= currentThronePrice takes it immediately; small buys never accumulate. Price is max(0.01 ETH, 1.2 * takeover payment * 2^(-reign seconds/3600)); an empty throne costs 0.01 ETH. Income accrues at second resolution, leaving approximately 98% of the pool per hour absent new fees, with fixed-point rounding and lazy accounting. Implementation trade-offs: income from each new reign vests only after five minutes; every earlier exit, including self-retakes and rival takeovers, forfeits provisional income. This limits short take-and-dump and relay farming but delays claimability relative to the brief. Vested booked income remains claimable after losing the throne. The king must retain takeover tokens; self-retakes preserve the larger old/new requirement. Any king sell via KingRouter checks holdings before escrow and immediately ends the reign. Permissionless dethrone() rejects an empty throne or sufficient balance. Swaps and claims also check holdings. A detected shortfall returns provisional income and forfeits the unverified interval since last accrual, preserving vested booked credits. Only KingRouter hookData, abi.encode(msg.sender, mustTake), authenticates the buyer; output goes to that wallet, including contract wallets. mustTake reverts the whole buy if the game is closed or its executed gross ETH is below price. Foreign routers pay fees but cannot crown buyers; canonical 64-byte mustTake=true data from them reverts. Foreign-router surplus sells cannot be attributed; shortfalls may only be detected later. Transfers out and restoration between observations are undetectable. These limits do not enforce immediate dethroning on every arbitrary-router sell. Five-minute farming can still profit; mustTake prevents paying swap fees after losing a takeover race, but ordering, sandwiching, block stuffing and sequencer censorship remain risks. Views expose king, reignStart, requiredBalance, poolSize, currentThronePrice, nextHalvingTime (0 at floor/empty), incomePerHour, unclaimedIncome, kingReignEarnings, kingVestingIncome, throne and paginated getReigns history. Initial price is 10000 * 2^96, since currency1/currency0 = 100,000,000 KING per ETH: 10 ETH total-supply market cap. Requested 90% single-sided KING liquidity below the current tick and 0% requester allocation are governed by separately versioned launch policy; this manifest cannot set allocations or chain.
